title: Inconsistent IoFailure boundary type between pkix-aia and pkix-truststore
description:
Both pkix-aia and pkix-truststore need to represent I/O errors in a Clone+Eq+Serialize-friendly shape (AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 forbids embedding raw `std::io::Error`). Both crates independently implement the same pattern:

- pkix-aia: `AiaError::IoFailure { kind: std::io::ErrorKind, message: String }` as an enum variant, with a private `io_error_kind_serde` module for round-tripping `ErrorKind` via its Debug label.
- pkix-truststore: `pub struct IoFailure { pub kind: io::ErrorKind, pub message: String }` as a standalone public struct, with its own `io_error_kind_serde` module using the same Debug-label technique.

The two implementations are functionally identical but:
1. pkix-aia inlines the fields as an enum variant; pkix-truststore extracts a named struct.
2. Both ship separate copies of the `io_error_kind_serde` serialize/deserialize logic (identical label match tables for the same set of ErrorKind variants).
3. A caller working with both AiaError and pkix_truststore::IoFailure cannot use one conversion for both.

Impact: Code duplication across the io_error_kind_serde modules — currently ~70 lines each of identical match-arm tables. When a new Rust ErrorKind variant is added, both tables need updating independently. A shared boundary type or a shared serde helper module would eliminate the duplication.

Locations: /home/mark/PROJECT/PKIX/pkix-aia/src/lib.rs lines 264-437 (io_error_kind_serde module), /home/mark/PROJECT/PKIX/pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs lines 221-336 (IoFailure struct + io_error_kind_serde module)
